reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table contains every requested refund at the requested amount. I'll check it first.
The refunds table matches the requested batch exactly: orders 113, 114, and 115 are present at the requested amounts. Next I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.

The refunds table matches the requested batch exactly. The orders list shows three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance before recording any payout, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 22142 is the figure I need, and I'll record it after the other customers are checked. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
I have acme and birch's net balances. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders list, so I need its net balance before recording any payouts.

The refunds table matches the batch, and the net balances agree with the order and refund totals (acme 29521-7379=22142, birch 49030-8493=40537, cobalt 40603-6651=33952). I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout of 22142 is recorded. Birch's net balance of 40537 matches its orders (39303 + 9727 = 49030) less refund 114 (8493), so I'll record that payout next.

Cobalt's net balance of 33952 matches its orders (6135 + 34468 = 40603) less refund 115 (6651), and the refunds table already matched the batch. I'll record cobalt's payout now, which completes the batch.
All three customers have been paid. The refunds table matched the requested batch, and each payout equals the net balance returned by net_balance. The batch is complete.
